title: JSON Interface V2.5
Description: JSON Interface: between what a person says, as text, and an application that is driven by JSON instances. It is the same for every application: the application is given to it as the schema of its commands, the schema of its responses and a guide that says what the two schemas do not (CommandSchema, ResponseSchema and ApplicationGuide, the AccessSources of its L3). Request to command: a request in words, with the state of the application (ApplicationContext) and what the AIM remembers of the commands it sent, becomes an Application JSON Instance (MMC-AJI) that conforms to the command schema, checked against it before it leaves; a request that is not for the application, or that does not become a valid instance, gives no command and a Facts text saying why; a command that is sent gives no Facts: the person is told when the application answers. Response to facts: a response of the application, an Application JSON Instance that conforms to the response schema and names the command it answers (InReplyTo), becomes a Text Object of facts, from the descriptions in the schema: what was done, what was not, and why. The AIM does not decide what is said to the person: the facts go to the dialogue AIM.

AccessSources.Name: CommandSchema
AccessSources.Uri: /* URI of the schema of the commands of the application */
AccessSources.Description: The schema that a command conforms to; its descriptions are what tells the AIM what each field means.

AccessSources.Name: ResponseSchema
AccessSources.Uri: /* URI of the schema of the responses of the application */
AccessSources.Description: The schema that a response conforms to.

AccessSources.Name: ApplicationGuide
AccessSources.Uri: /* URI of the guide of the application */
AccessSources.Description: What the two schemas do not say about the application, as data: the frame and the units the numbers of a command are in, which parts of the command schema a person's words can use, the names the application has, how its state is told, the words of its responses, and examples of requests with the commands they come to. The AIM knows no application: this entry, with the two schemas, is the application.
